title: Running AV Reasoning Models Within Onboard Compute and Latency Limits | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA released Alpamayo 2 Edge, a 2B-parameter Nemotron-based adaptive-reasoning vision-language-action driving model that runs at 160–190 ms pixel-to-trajectory latency on DRIVE AGX Thor, post-trained with closed-loop RL in AlpaGym (+48.9% driving performance). It also released AlpaJudge, a human-calibrated reasoning evaluator/reward model, with workflows for scoring, data selection and RL rewards; early partners PORT, Niulinx and Embedl report fast real-vehicle and real-time deployment.

insights.claim: NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Edge is an adaptive-reasoning vision-language-action model built on the 2B Nemotron-based backbone of Cosmos 3 Edge plus a diffusion action expert, designed for real-time onboard driving on NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor.
insights.speaker: Marco Pavone
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is pushing reasoning VLA autonomy into production vehicle compute, strengthening the Thor platform's software pull for OEMs.
insights.locator: NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Edge addresses this need

insights.claim: Alpamayo 2 Edge reasons adaptively, emitting special <NOMINAL> tokens instead of Chain-of-Causation reasoning traces during routine driving to conserve onboard inference compute.
insights.speaker: Marco Pavone
insights.so_what: Adaptive reasoning is a template for fitting LLM-style reasoning into fixed edge compute budgets — relevant to automotive and robotics silicon sizing.
insights.locator: In particular, note that the model will now

insights.claim: Alpamayo 2 Edge is distilled offline from Chain-of-Causation reasoning autolabels generated by the larger Alpamayo 2 Super, and uses multi-resolution surround-view inputs and DFlash2 speculative decoding for efficiency.
insights.speaker: Marco Pavone
insights.so_what: Large-teacher/small-student pipeline means datacenter GPU training feeds edge deployment — NVIDIA monetizes both ends.

insights.claim: Closed-loop reinforcement learning post-training in NVIDIA AlpaGym improved Alpamayo 2 Edge's closed-loop driving performance by 48.9% over the best checkpoint without closed-loop RL.
insights.speaker: Marco Pavone
insights.so_what: Simulation-based closed-loop RL is a major performance lever for AV — increases demand for simulation compute.
insights.quote: improving closed-loop driving performance by 48.9% on top of the best-performing checkpoint without closed-loop RL
insights.locator: Alpamayo 2 Edge is post-trained with closed-loop

insights.claim: Alpamayo 2 Edge (2B) is reported to achieve approximately 40x the distance between at-fault incidents in AlpaSim compared with the 4B Qwen-Drive-1.0.
insights.speaker: Marco Pavone
insights.so_what: NVIDIA positions its open AV model as ahead of a Chinese-origin rival at half the parameter count; vendor-run benchmark, treat with caution.

insights.claim: Optimized via FP8 calibration, ONNX export and TensorRT Edge-LLM engines with DFlash2, Alpamayo 2 Edge reaches 160 ms to 190 ms pixel-to-trajectory latency on DRIVE AGX Thor-X depending on how much reasoning it generates.
insights.speaker: Marco Pavone
insights.so_what: Sub-200 ms reasoning-based planning on Thor supports the case for reasoning VLAs in L2+/L4 stacks on NVIDIA silicon.
insights.quote: the resulting optimized model has a pixel-to-trajectory inference latency of 160 ms to 190 ms depending on the amount of reasoning

insights.claim: PORT reported that in early simulation tests Alpamayo 2 Edge kept its lane in more than twice as many runs as Alpamayo 1.5, recovered from lane offsets about 40% more often, and planned roughly twice as fast as its hand-tuned Alpamayo 1.5 server on the same GPU.
insights.speaker: Marco Pavone
insights.so_what: Generation-over-generation gains suggest rapid improvement in NVIDIA's open AV model line.
insights.locator: Within days of getting early access

insights.claim: Niulinx reported Alpamayo 2 Edge reduced displacement error (minADE) by 13.6% and 3-second lateral RMSE by 46.1% versus Alpamayo 2 Super zero-shot on its differing sensor setup, with fine-tuning on its own data cutting displacement error a further 44.2%.
insights.speaker: Marco Pavone
insights.so_what: Cross-sensor generalization lowers adoption cost for smaller AV developers building on NVIDIA's open models.

insights.claim: Embedl reported getting Alpamayo 2 Edge running at 10 Hz on AGX Thor for real-time planning in under 48 hours.
insights.speaker: Marco Pavone
insights.so_what: Fast time-to-deploy for third-party optimizers broadens the Thor ecosystem.
insights.quote: In less than 48 hours, we made NVIDIA’s Alpamayo 2 Edge run at 10 Hz on AGX Thor for real-time planning.

insights.claim: NVIDIA AlpaJudge is a human-calibrated evaluator and reward model with a reference-based variant (returns one alignment probability from text) and a reference-free variant (scores a rationale from six camera frames and meta-action context using five rubric probabilities: agreement, safety, grounding, completeness, causal consistency).
insights.speaker: Marco Pavone
insights.so_what: Reasoning-quality evaluation becomes a measurable, trainable objective for AV — a building block toward explainability for regulators.

insights.claim: AlpaJudge-RF combines its rubric as overall = 0.6 × action + 0.4 × component, where action = p_match × (1 + p_safe)/2 and component is the mean of grounding, completeness and causal-consistency probabilities.
insights.speaker: Marco Pavone
insights.so_what: Weighting puts action correctness/safety ahead of explanation quality.
insights.locator: Run the notebook’s fixed construction-zone sample

insights.claim: Mid-range judge scores often mark the most informative training data, while very low scores may be mislabeled, failed or genuinely hard rare cases that should be reviewed rather than discarded and very high scores indicate scenes the model has already learned.
insights.speaker: Marco Pavone
insights.so_what: Score-based data curation is a reusable approach to improve data efficiency in AV and robotics training.
insights.locator: AlpaJudge’s score is useful for training data selection

insights.claim: A reasoning reward from AlpaJudge-RB can be plugged into open-loop GRPO training alongside trajectory error and comfort, but the reward should keep its trajectory gate so the policy cannot earn high reward from a fluent but wrong driving explanation.
insights.speaker: Marco Pavone
insights.so_what: Highlights reward-hacking risk when optimizing for explanation quality in safety-critical systems.
insights.quote: so the policy is less likely to earn a high total reward from a fluent but wrong driving explanation
